clustering.caveat: Silhouette is measured on the original embedding space but the clusters were found in a 10-D UMAP projection, which is not optimised for it, so low values are expected. With few clusters it mostly reflects one split; a largest-cluster share near 1 means the map found one topic, not sub-topics. Judge cluster quality by reading the labels.

retrieval.judged_by: THREE AI RATERS, majority vote - still NOT human. (1) a first pass by Claude from title + ~210 characters of abstract; (2) and (3) two independent Claude subagents (fresh context, instructed not to read the project or each other) that judged every candidate from the FULL abstract with the same rubric. Agreement over 294 query-candidate pairs (Cohen's kappa): first-pass vs A 0.787, first-pass vs B 0.79, A vs B 0.905; 54 pairs were unanimously relevant and 27 were disputed (decided by majority; listed per query under 'disputed'). Rubric: relevant if a researcher searching the query would want to read the paper because it substantially addresses the query topic; passing mentions do not count. Raters were all language models, so shared blind spots are possible. The first-pass labels are kept under 'relevant_first_pass_claude'. data/eval/REVIEW.md lists what a human should confirm.
retrieval.caveat: Relevance is judged over the pooled top results of these same four modes, so a relevant paper none of them retrieved is invisible to every metric (pooling bias). Recall is therefore recall within the pool, not recall over the whole literature.

refusal_end_to_end.judged_by: Claude (AI), PROVISIONAL - labels in data/eval/questions.json (not a human judgement)
unanswerable_that_were_answered: How does reinforcement learning from human feedback train a reward model?
How do transformers implement multi-head self-attention?
refusal_end_to_end.reading_of_those: Both answers were grounded in real passages and, after a scope rule was added to the prompt, are explicitly attributed to the specific paper's setting ('In the context of the ... paper', 'RLHF for RAG systems'). The labels 'unanswerable' are debatable for them: the collection does contain text on both topics, in a narrower setting.
refusal_end_to_end.decision: REFUSAL_TAU stays unset: the model's own INSUFFICIENT_CONTEXT refusal (plus 'no retrieval hits' and 'no valid citation') is the active mechanism; a score threshold would falsely refuse answerable questions for little gain

retrieval_bootstrap.mrr_scope: MRR here is over the 14 queries with a relevant paper; the 'retrieval' section's MRR counts all 15 judged queries (a query with no relevant paper scores 0), so the two differ
retrieval_bootstrap.method: paired bootstrap over queries, 5000 resamples, 95% percentile interval of the mean difference; Wilcoxon signed-rank p-value alongside (scipy, two-sided)
retrieval_bootstrap.judged_by: THREE AI RATERS, majority vote - still NOT human. (1) a first pass by Claude from title + ~210 characters of abstract; (2) and (3) two independent Claude subagents (fresh context, instructed not to read the project or each other) that judged every candidate from the FULL abstract with the same rubric. Agreement over 294 query-candidate pairs (Cohen's kappa): first-pass vs A 0.787, first-pass vs B 0.79, A vs B 0.905; 54 pairs were unanimously relevant and 27 were disputed (decided by majority; listed per query under 'disputed'). Rubric: relevant if a researcher searching the query would want to read the paper because it substantially addresses the query topic; passing mentions do not count. Raters were all language models, so shared blind spots are possible. The first-pass labels are kept under 'relevant_first_pass_claude'. data/eval/REVIEW.md lists what a human should confirm.
retrieval_bootstrap.caveat: Descriptive, not a hypothesis test: 6 comparisons are made with no multiple-comparison correction, on only 14 queries, where a percentile bootstrap can undercover (intervals may be too narrow), so 'excludes_zero' is a description of the interval, not significance. The candidate pool the labels were built on comes from these same retrieval modes, and the labels are provisional (not human). An interval that includes zero means 'not distinguishable here', not 'equal'.

unsupported_claims.sentence: Iterative retrieval assists multi-hop question answering by generating intermediate reasoning steps that help address complex questions [2][3].
unsupported_claims.why: Intermediate reasoning steps are LLM CoT, not stated as what iterative retrieval does.

unsupported_claims.sentence: Iterative retrieval helps multi-hop question answering by generating intermediate reasoning steps, which allows the model to leverage external data sources to compensate for missing internal knowledge or erroneous retrieval [2].

faithfulness.judged_by: two independent Claude subagents against the FULL cited passage (strict: every material part must be in the passage); the 2 disagreements were broken by Claude reading the passages. AI judgement, NOT human.
faithfulness.sample: 40 cited answer sentences drawn with a fixed seed (7) from the 52 stored non-refused answers of this collection
faithfulness.reading: the failure mode is a sentence that attributes to retrieval something the passage credits to another mechanism (chain-of-thought) - the citation is real, the causal link is the model's gloss
